reason: Confirmed in jsdom (StrictMode list of keyed children with mount/unmount effects, reordered: react-dom 19.2.6 re-runs the moved children's effect cleanup and setup in DEV, 19.3.1 runs none), but it is DEV-only double invocation that production never did, so code written for 19.2 is the same as for 19.3 and only code expecting effects to re-run when a child merely moves would notice, which no plausible application relies on.

As v3 found, and re-checked against react-dom 19.2.6: the shorthandToLonghand table (19.3.1 adds borderBlock/borderInline*, inset*, container, fontSynthesis and others) is read only by the DEV-only console.error about conflicting shorthand/longhand style updates in react-dom-client.development.js, has no reference in the production build, and the styles applied to the DOM are the same, so the change only alters which combinations log a warning.

react-dom 19.2.6 already included the submitter (createFormDataWithSubmitter inserted a temporary input with its name/value), so in jsdom a form action with named <button name=intent value=save/publish> submitters and an unnamed button gets identical FormData on 19.2.6 and 19.3.1, and the only difference from passing the submitter to new FormData() is an <input type=image> submitter (name= before, name.x/name.y now), which no plausible application code relies on reading as an empty name= entry.

As v3 found against 19.1.0, and re-checked against react-dom 19.2.6, whose recoverFromConcurrentError still commits an error-recovery retry that ends RootSuspendedAtTheShell (19.3.1 adds the RootSuspendedAtTheShell check, PR #36911): this is the client's recovery render, and the old behavior's only observable effect is a later "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" crash when a recovery render suspends on use() without a Suspense boundary, so code written for 19.2 is the same as for 19.3 and no plausible application code depends on the old behavior.

As v3 found against 19.1.0, and re-checked against react-dom 19.2.6, which has the same number-specific code (setDefaultValue skips a focused type=number input, and a focusout handler syncs it later): the only difference is when a focused number input's value attribute/defaultValue is updated, which displayed values and form reset only reveal in a focused-then-reset-without-re-render corner, and code written for 19.2 is the same JSX as for 19.3, so no plausible application code depends on the old behavior.

Preact 11.0.1 calls parentDom.moveBefore() only when the DOM implements it (diff/children.js) and otherwise falls back to insertBefore as 10.x does; jsdom 30 has no Element.moveBefore and the state it preserves (focus, iframe content, running animations) needs a real browser, so observing the change needs a browser.
A raised minimum browser baseline (Chrome 71 / Safari 12.1 / Firefox 69 / Edge 79, IE11 dropped) with no API change, which nothing an agent writes in a Node/jsdom TypeScript project can observe.

Diffing lazyInitializer in react 19.2.6 and 19.3.1, PR #34906 only changes the DEV-only debug info (payload._ioInfo.value, read by DevTools and Performance Tracks) to resolve to the module's .default instead of the module object; the production build has no _ioInfo, lazy() still returns moduleObject.default to render, and in jsdom a lazy component and its resolved component keep the same identity behavior on both versions.

As v3 found, re-checked against 4.24.14 (the last release before 2026-06-01): the only difference in core/lib/oauth/checks.js is that the state/PKCE/nonce cookies now store provider: options.provider.id and use() throws when another provider handles the callback, and in every working multi-provider flow (two providers for one IdP, renamed provider ids) the cookie is minted and consumed by the same provider, so only forged or cross-provider callbacks and sign-ins in flight across the upgrade are rejected, which no application code relies on.

Not S3: astro 7.4.1 depends on cookie 2.0.1 (installed in the template) and Astro.cookies.set() serializes with its stringifySetCookie; compared with astro 6.4.2 (cookie 1.1.1), values like user@example.com, a/b:c=d and base64 now appear raw in Set-Cookie instead of percent-encoded, while JSON, spaces and % are encoded as before, and every value round-trips identically through Astro.cookies.get(), cookie's parser and decodeURIComponent, so code written for 6.x reads the same values and only code comparing raw header bytes or form-decoding '+' as a space would notice, which no plausible application relies on.
